title: The memorial at Steilneset
sentences: And in that, but but the building itself, the building you're talking about, this long building,
so there's an architect, a recognised architect too, who you have to tell us who made it.
Yes, the Steilneset memorial, which is a memorial for the victims of the witchcraft trials in Finnmark, is built from three components.
Art is this installation that stands in a glass pavilion, a free-standing glass pavilion, and there's a burning chair there.
Above the chair seven oval mirrors are mounted, which reflect the object in the middle, reflect the chair from different angles.
So you get this very strongly, that when you reflect an object,
it's the angle of that reflection that determines what you see in this mirror.
And those who walk around this installation, around this chair that has a five-fingered flame in the middle,
they themselves also get caught in one of the mirrors, so you're no longer a spectator, but you're actually a participant.
And it poses this very difficult question: how would you have found yourself in the seventeenth century if you had lived at that time
and been involved in accusations against alleged witches.
The other building at Steilneset is a hundred and fifty, a hundred and thirty-five metre long building, a funnel, a long corridor,
and this corridor, you walk through the whole corridor with memorial plaques on both sides.
It isn't that wide, so you can't get away.
Two can walk side by side,
so you get these memorial plaques about the 91 victims very close to you,
and whether you walk fast or slowly you can't avoid seeing here there are a great many names, here are individual people.
And you also can't avoid seeing that there's a strong repetition of the sentence, namely to fire and pyre.
